title: The Sanhedrin
lead: The Jewish high council in Jerusalem in the time of Jesus and the apostles, led by the high priest and made up of chief priests, elders and scribes, Sadducees and Pharisees. The Gospels and Acts set the trials of Jesus, Peter and John, Stephen and Paul before it; the Mishnah later describes it in idealized form.

sections.b: The Greek synedrion means a "sitting together," a council. In Jerusalem it was the leading Jewish court and governing body under Roman rule, presided over by the high priest (Matthew 26:57–59; Acts 5:21, 27). Josephus uses the word for councils of several kinds. Its exact powers under Rome are debated, above all whether it could carry out a death sentence (John 18:31). The Mishnah tractate Sanhedrin, compiled about AD 200, describes a court of seventy-one, modeled on the seventy elders who shared Moses' burden with Moses at their head (Numbers 11:16; Mishnah Sanhedrin 1:6), with detailed rules, but much of it reflects the ideals of later rabbis rather than the practice of the first century.
